Jared: Quick weekly cache + batching snapshot for AcmeCo
Jared: Short summary: cache hit rate fell, batching roughly steady, cost/1k tokens up. Need a couple quick ops before renewal meeting.
Priya: Can you drop the exact metrics?
Jared: 7d window vs previous 7d:
Jared: • Cache (prefix/KV) hit rate: 54% (prev 70%)
Jared: • Avg batch size (reqs/forward): 4.0 (prev 4.4)
Jared: • Cost / 1k tokens: $0.29 (prev $0.21)
Jared: • P50 latency: 120ms (flat)
Jared: • P95 latency: 355ms (up from 260ms)
Jared: • 5xx inference errors: 0.5% (short spike during autoscale event)
Miguel: Is the hit-rate drop concentrated on any route or model?
Jared: Filtered: /v1/chat hit 46%, /v1/generate hit 76% — chat is the low one.
Nora: Did Acme change prompts or session behavior recently?
Jared: They shipped a dynamic system prompt tweak last Tues that likely mutated cache keys for chat sessions.
Priya: That would explain the sudden key churn. How much of the cost bump is from the cache regression vs the error retries?
Miguel: Rough split: ~70% of the cost delta tied to lower cache hit, remainder from retry/recompute during the 5xx spike.
Jared: I ran a quick simulation: canonicalizing cache keys back to stable values would restore ~12-15% hit and cut cost ~9%. Increasing batching window from 10ms→20ms on chat yields +0.8 batch size and ~11% cost reduction but raises p95 ~55ms.
Priya: Their SLA is p95 < 400ms; 355ms → ~410ms would violate SLA, but if current p95 is 355 and batching adds 55ms we'd go to 410. Need careful canary.
Miguel: Options: 1) Ask Acme to revert/standardize system prompt (low impact), 2) Temporarily bump chat batching window with canary, 3) Warm cache for top sessions, 4) Short capacity buffer if autoscale hiccups recur.
Jared: I can coordinate pre-warming for top 100 sessions with Acme PM tomorrow.
Nora: Any correlation between the 5xx OOMs and batching?
Jared: Logs show OOM on attention kernel during a brief oversubscription around Thu 03:10 UTC when autoscaler scaled down too quickly. Deploy bot posted scale event.
Miguel: For the batching change I'll run a 10% canary first and watch p95/errors for 45m. If stable, ramp to 100% over 30m.
Miguel: Proposed runtime patch (canary) snippet:
Miguel: ```json
Miguel: {
Miguel:   "route": "/v1/chat",
Miguel:   "batching": {
Miguel:     "window_ms": 20,
Miguel:     "max_batch": 20
Miguel:   },
Miguel:   "notes": "temp increase to offset cache regression"
Miguel: }
Miguel: ```
Priya: Cost tradeoff if we add a short capacity buffer vs doing nothing?
Miguel: Extra GPU reserve ~ $550/day. Batching+cache fixes estimated to save ~$380/day at current traffic. So buffer for 48h mostly neutral if fixes are applied quickly.
Jared: Plan suggestion: 1) Ask Acme to rollback/normalize system prompt keys immediately (owner: Acme-Eng, I'll ping). 2) Start batching canary at 10% (owner: Miguel). 3) Prewarm top sessions (owner: Jared). 4) Hold a 48h capacity buffer only if prompt normalization stalls or errors persist (owner: Nora to watch).
Priya: Assigning owners as above. Also note renewal check-in in 11 days per acme-bot.
acme-bot: Reminder: Renewal kickoff in 11 days. :calendar:
Jared: I'll update this thread after pinging Acme-Eng; aim to have canary ready by EOD.
Nora: I'll watch p95 + 5xx dashboards and post alerts if we cross thresholds.
Miguel: I'll prep the runtime diff and canary plan, include rollback steps.
Jared: If Acme refuses prompt change, we will prioritize batching + targeted cache warms and revisit TTLs.
Priya: Good. If hit rate still <60% after prompt normalization, schedule deeper sessionization and tokenization review with ML infra.
Jared: Update will be here by EOD tomorrow.
Jared: — end thread —
